question: Do the 2010 Tayabas River survey's taxon labels align with current fish-name backbones, and are any labels ambiguous?

sourceContext.bibliography: Paller, V. G. V., Corpuz, M. N. C., & Ocampo, P. P. (2013). Diversity and distribution of freshwater fish assemblages in Tayabas River, Quezon (Philippines). Philippine Journal of Science, 142(1), 55-67.
sourceContext.studyScope: The paper reports a 2010 survey of nine stations across upstream, midstream and downstream reaches, sampled during three-day periods in February and September. It reports 15 taxa in aggregate. It does not provide a station-by-taxon-to-current-municipality crosswalk in the reviewed table text.
sourceContext.sourceTextCaveat: Only minimal name-status deltas are recorded here. The complete species table and its abundance/station cells are not reproduced. The text extraction reads one pipefish label as Dorichthys martensii; direct PDF download was blocked by an anti-bot challenge, so that spelling was not visually verified from a locally rendered page.
sourceContext.seasonConflict: The article assigns February to wet season and September to dry season, while also describing November-April as the dry period. Season-specific results remain unmapped to months.

taxonomyReferences.provider: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, species matching API v1
limits: The GBIF Backbone is continuously maintained; this match snapshot is not tied to a fixed release.
A strict name match does not validate the source authors' fish identification, voucher, locality, habitat, or collection status.

taxonomyReferences.provider: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, California Academy of Sciences
taxonomyReferences.accessReview: Search-indexed catalog excerpts were available; direct page open returned HTTP 403.
taxonomyReferences.role: Independent nomenclatural cross-check only; not local occurrence evidence or specimen validation.

minimalDeltas.catalogCrossCheck: The Catalog of Fishes lists the current status as valid as Barbodes binotatus.
minimalDeltas.decision: Keep the article's historical name attached to the 2010 source record; retain Barbodes binotatus only as a nomenclatural candidate. This does not re-identify specimens.

minimalDeltas.strictGbifMatch: No usage returned for the text-extracted spelling.
minimalDeltas.gbifCandidateCrossCheck: A strict GBIF query for Microphis martensii returned no usage, while Doryichthys martensii matched as accepted.
minimalDeltas.decision: Do not silently correct the source label or choose a current combination. Resolve the table spelling visually and reconcile the different backbone treatments before any species-level projection.

minimalDeltas.gbifResult: No strict usage returned for the genus-plus-spelling qualifier.
minimalDeltas.decision: Retain as an unresolved genus-level source label; do not assign it to a species.

findings.otherExactMatches: The remaining 12 source-name queries returned accepted species-rank GBIF usages with confidence values of 98-99. They remain name matches only; individual source table cells are not transcribed here.

rightsAndEvidenceDecision.journalAccess: PJS describes its online journal as open access, but its current author guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form.
rightsAndEvidenceDecision.reason: The crosswalk identifies nomenclatural candidates but cannot verify fish specimens, site-level allocation, current presence, or source reuse rights. The historical survey remains research context only.

nextActions: Seek item-specific reuse terms before extracting the source table into a project checklist.
Ask the UPLB Museum of Natural History whether this survey's deposited vouchers have catalog numbers and a public record crosswalk; no inquiry has been sent.
If permission and voucher identities are confirmed, reconcile the pipefish spelling and taxonomy, then map only source-supported reach/date cells without inferring current presence.
